Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0118", "row_sha256": "d123453652fd61b96b7762d6ac3fb6bf3e0a884ae3386657606808b25c938757", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you help get the film society's message ready for this week? we're planning a screening of the short film Paper Moons on Thursday, October 17, at 7:30 p.m. in Arts Hall, but the distributor's written screening permission still needs to come through. please make the message depend on whether we've received that permission by Monday at noon. if it's confirmed by then, write a friendly member email, no more than 120 words, announcing the screening and giving the film title, date, time, and place. if it hasn't been confirmed by Monday at noon, don't announce the screening or make it sound like it's definitely happening. instead, write a brief internal note to the society committee asking someone to follow up with the distributor and saying promotion should wait for written permission. We need to avoid sending members mixed signals while the committee is preparing this week's communications, so choose the right one of those two texts based on the permission status. keep whichever version clear and easy to send as written, and please return only that one text with no explanation or extra heading.", "output": "Prepare the film society's message for this week based on whether the distributor's written screening permission for *Paper Moons* has been confirmed by Monday at noon.

- If permission has been confirmed by then, write a friendly email to members announcing the screening on Thursday, October 17, at 7:30 p.m. in Arts Hall. Keep it to no more than 120 words and include the film title, date, time, and place.
- If permission has not been confirmed by Monday at noon, do not announce the screening or imply that it is definitely happening. Instead, write a brief internal note to the society committee asking someone to follow up with the distributor and stating that promotion should wait for written permission.

Return only the applicable text, ready to send, with no explanation or extra heading."}]
